environment: Windows x64, Chrome 153 headless, document.visibilityState=visible, Vite production build, same browser process, no CPU throttling requested
method: One initial table render excluded, then five successive row appends per case. Baseline is the pre-fix single-block MarkdownContent path, excluding its boundary-worker overhead. Worker case uses the real production StreamingMarkdownContent and module worker. Samples rounded to 0.1 ms.

metrics.pushMs: Synchronous flushSync(render) wall time for the incoming text update, not total parsing cost
metrics.formatReadyMs: Time until expected table rows are present plus next animation frame; excludes the explicit 20ms observation delay
metrics.maxTimerDelayMs: Largest excess delay of a 10ms heartbeat in each sample, including worker response/DOM work
metrics.renderMs: Not reported: React Profiler is disabled in production

limitations: Synthetic large-table fixture, not an end-to-end native Tauri measurement or a latency percentile from production traffic.
Only five measured updates per case; cold worker/JIT and machine scheduling affect dispersion.
Formatting readiness is slower in this measurement. New text remains immediately visible as literal provisional source until the worker formats it.
Initial mount, sustained faster-than-parser traffic, peak memory and power usage are not quantified by this benchmark. Coalescing/correctness are covered by separate tests.

An earlier development-server measurement (54KB push 184.8 to 26.9 ms) was an intermediate implementation and is not the final performance claim. Visible-browser attempts later became occluded/hidden and were discarded; final numbers use a dedicated headless browser with visible document state.
